title: 1957 AHSME Problem 20
statement: A man makes a trip by automobile at an average speed of \(50\) mph. He returns over the same route at an average speed of \(45\) mph. His average speed for the entire trip is:

solutions.text:
Let each leg have distance \(d.\) The average speed, in miles per hour, is \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{2d}{\frac{d}{50}+\frac{d}{45}} &=\frac{2}{\frac{1}{50}+\frac{1}{45}}\\ &=\frac{900}{19}\\ &=47\frac7{19}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Use a convenient one-way distance and divide total distance by total time
For equal distances the arithmetic mean of the two speeds is not the average speed
